To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have discovered a new type of antibiotics that feature an unusual sulfonyl-bridge between two aromatic substructures.

we discovered three novel, sulfonyl bridged alkaloid dimmers, named sulfadixiamycines A-C, and that we elucidated the biosynthesis of the compounds, revealing a radical-based three-component reaction catalyzed by flavoenzyme XiaH.

the xiamycin biosynthetic gene cluster is capable of generating novel, fully unprecedented, sulfa-drug-like antibiotics by flavoenzyme-mediated sulfur dioxide capture.

flavoenzyme-mediated sulfur dioxide capture represents a new strategy for the biosynthesis of unusual sulfur-containing natural products, including sulfonamides, sulfones, and sulfonate esters.
